name: Citizenship by Exceptional Presidential Grant

qualifying_event.description: The President of Georgia may grant citizenship, at full discretion and without the ordinary residence/language/history-test requirements, to a person who has made an exceptional contribution to Georgia or where it is in the state's interest -- including, per the source, persons residing in occupied territories, and persons making substantial economic investments in Georgia.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Demonstrated exceptional merit, state-interest justification, or a substantial economic investment, at the President's sole discretion -- no fixed, published qualifying threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a discretionary grant by the President of Georgia for exceptional contribution or state interest; there is no fixed, published investment amount or objective qualifying formula.

evidence_required.document: Case-specific evidence of exceptional contribution, state interest, or investment (no fixed checklist)

sources.title: Legislative Herald of Georgia (matsne.gov.ge) -- Organic Law of Georgia on Georgian Citizenship, Article 17

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Georgia's initial build -- included deliberately, similar to Cyprus's discontinued CBI route, because 'substantial economic investment' is explicitly named in the law as a ground the President may act on, making this Georgia's closest analogue to a citizenship-by-investment scheme, even though it is NOT a guaranteed, formula-based program the way Dominica's CBI is. STATUS SET TO DRAFT deliberately, not because sourcing is weak (the source IS tier-1) but because the qualifying_event itself is genuinely discretionary and unformulaic -- there is no fixed investment amount, timeline, or approval rate to model as a hard pass/fail test, and evidence_required difficulty is marked 'often_impossible' to reflect that an ordinary applicant cannot self-assess eligibility the way they can for the other routes in this build. dual_citizenship_allowed set true: this is one of the two cases (per Article 3(3)) where dual citizenship IS permitted, unlike ordinary naturalisation.
